title: Bones of the skull (anterior)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender, with surface detail added by an image model.

rows: Location
Forehead and the roofs of the orbits.
Articulates with
Parietal bones at the coronal suture, and the sphenoid, ethmoid, nasal, lacrimal, and zygomatic bones and the maxillae.
Features
Supraorbital margin with its notch or foramen. The frontal sinuses lie within the bone.
Location
Lower jaw. It is the only freely movable bone of the skull.
Articulates with
Temporal bones, at the two temporomandibular joints.
Features
Body, angle, and ramus. Coronoid and condylar processes. The mandibular foramen, where the inferior alveolar nerve enters, and the mental foramen.
Location
Center of the skull base, behind the orbits. It is shaped like a butterfly.
Articulates with
Frontal, parietal, temporal, occipital, and ethmoid bones, and the zygomatic and palatine bones and the vomer.
Features
Body, greater and lesser wings, and pterygoid processes. The body has the sphenoidal sinuses and the sella turcica, which holds the pituitary gland.
hy: Its openings and what passes through: optic canal (CN II, ophthalmic artery), superior orbital fissure (CN III, IV, V1, VI), foramen rotundum (V2), foramen ovale (V3), foramen spinosum (middle meningeal artery).

rows: Location
In the midline between the orbits. It forms part of the roof and side walls of the nasal cavity and part of the medial wall of each orbit.
Articulates with
Frontal and sphenoid bones, the nasal, lacrimal, and palatine bones, the maxillae, the inferior nasal conchae, and the vomer.
Features
Cribriform plate with the crista galli, perpendicular plate, ethmoidal air cells, and superior and middle nasal conchae. The perpendicular plate forms the upper part of the nasal septum.
hy: The fibers of the olfactory nerve pass through the cribriform plate. A fracture here can cause loss of smell and leakage of cerebrospinal fluid from the nose.

rows: Location
Thin plate of bone in the midline that forms the lower, back part of the nasal septum.
Articulates with
Sphenoid, the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid, both maxillae, and both palatine bones.
Location
Side and roof of the cranial vault, one on each side.
Articulates with

Frontal bone at the coronal suture, the opposite parietal bone at the sagittal suture, the occipital bone at the lambdoid suture, the temporal bone at the squamous suture, and the greater wing of the sphenoid.
Location
Side and base of the skull, around the ear.
Articulates with
Parietal, occipital, sphenoid, and zygomatic bones, and the mandible at the temporomandibular joint.
Features
Squamous, petrous, mastoid, and tympanic parts and the styloid process. The petrous part houses the middle and inner ear.
hy: At the pterion the frontal, parietal, temporal, and sphenoid bones meet and the skull is thin. A fracture here can tear the middle meningeal artery and cause an epidural hematoma.

Its openings and what passes through: internal acoustic meatus (CN VII and VIII), stylomastoid foramen (CN VII leaves the skull), and, between it and the occipital bone, the jugular foramen (CN IX, X, XI, and the internal jugular vein).

rows: Location
Cheekbone. It also forms part of the lateral wall and floor of the orbit.
Articulates with
Frontal bone, greater wing of the sphenoid, maxilla, and the zygomatic process of the temporal bone, with which it forms the zygomatic arch.
Location
Upper jaw. It forms most of the hard palate, the floor of the orbit, and the side wall of the nasal cavity.
Articulates with
Frontal, nasal, lacrimal, ethmoid, zygomatic, and palatine bones, the vomer, the inferior nasal concha, and the opposite maxilla.
Features
Maxillary sinus, infraorbital foramen, and the alveolar process that carries the upper teeth.
Location
Bridge of the nose, one on each side of the midline.
Articulates with
Frontal bone, the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid, the maxilla, and the opposite nasal bone.
Location
Front of the medial wall of the orbit. It is the smallest bone of the face.
Articulates with
Frontal bone, ethmoid, maxilla, and inferior nasal concha.
Features
With the maxilla it forms the fossa for the lacrimal sac and the start of the nasolacrimal canal.
Location
Curved bone on the side wall of the nasal cavity, below the middle concha. Unlike the superior and middle conchae, which are parts of the ethmoid, it is a separate bone.
Articulates with
Maxilla, lacrimal bone, ethmoid, and palatine bone.
Features
Covered by a thick mucous membrane that warms and moistens the air breathed in. The nasolacrimal duct opens under it, into the inferior meatus.
Location
Lower border of the maxilla, which forms the arch of the upper jaw.
Features
Holds the sockets of the upper teeth. It shrinks away when the teeth are lost.
Location
Horizontal, horseshoe-shaped front part of the mandible.
Features
Its upper border, the alveolar process, holds the lower teeth. The mental foramen opens on its outer surface below the second premolar. The mental nerve and vessels leave through it.
Location
Where the lower border of the body of the mandible meets the posterior border of the ramus.
Features
Masseter attaches to its outer surface and medial pterygoid to its inner surface.
Location
Upward projection of the zygomatic bone along the lateral margin of the orbit.
Features
Joins the zygomatic process of the frontal bone at the frontozygomatic suture.
Location
Thin plate that projects laterally from the front of the body of the sphenoid. It forms the back part of the roof of the orbit.
Features
The optic canal passes through its root and carries the optic nerve and the ophthalmic artery. The superior orbital fissure lies between it and the greater wing.
Location
Vertical plate that rises from the back of the body of the mandible on each side.
Features

It ends above in the coronoid process, where temporalis inserts, and the condylar process, which forms the temporomandibular joint. The mandibular foramen on its inner surface admits the inferior alveolar nerve and vessels.
Location
Lateral end of the supraorbital margin of the frontal bone.
Features
Runs down to join the frontal process of the zygomatic bone, completing the lateral margin of the orbit.
Location
Midline elevation on the front of the body of the mandible that forms the chin.
Features
It lies over the line where the two halves of the mandible fused in infancy, during the first one to two years of life.
